items.titleEn: Wall Street's bullish bets tick higher after gold bounces back above $3,600, Main Street maintains bearish bias with payrolls on deck
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold prices staged a sharp selloff followed by a strong recovery during the U.S. Thanksgiving-shortened trading week, with bargain-hunting and a weaker U.S. dollar helping the precious metal rebound from last week's steep losses after stronger economic data, persistent inflation, and expectations for another Federal Reserve rate hike drove prices to their lowest level in 15 months. Spot gold kicked off the week trading at $3,532.80 per ounce on Sunday evening, and the yellow metal rallied sharply on Monday as the dollar retreated from recent highs and buyers returned following the previous week's collapse toward $3,500. The rebound carried gold back above $3,600, with prices setting their weekly high at $3,689.08 per ounce on Monday before sellers returned as traders positioned themselves for Wednesday's inflation and economic growth reports. The recovery faded Tuesday after November consumer confidence jumped to 103.3, well above expectations, reinforcing the resilience of the U.S. economy and reducing immediate safe-haven demand. Selling then intensified Wednesday after October PCE inflation rose 3.8% annually and third-quarter GDP growth was revised higher to 4.3%, strengthening expectations that the Fed would raise rates again in December. Gold broke decisively below $3,500 in the wake of the data releases, and set its weekly low at $3,426.35 per ounce on Wednesday, its lowest level since August 2025.

items.titleEn: Gold climbs above $3,650, silver surges as Wall Street rebounds sharply - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were sharply higher in late U.S. trading Friday, extending their recovery from recent lows as a technology-led equity rally, improved investor risk appetite and renewed Chinese physical demand supported precious metals despite rising Treasury yields and a firmer dollar. Gold recovered above $3,650.00 an ounce after falling to a 14-month low earlier this week, while silver recorded substantially stronger gains as bargain hunting and renewed speculative demand accelerated the rebound. The advance coincided with Wall Street's strongest weekly performance since April 2025, although trading activity remained subdued following Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday. At 4:46 p.m. EST, spot gold was trading near $3,653.00 an ounce, up $87.50, or 2.45%, while silver was trading near $43.620, up $2.205, or 5.32%, on the session. Gold traded between $3,569.60 and $3,686.00 during the day, while silver's range extended from $41.630 to $44.690. The latest U.S. economic figures continued to highlight the resilience of the American economy despite persistent inflation and signs of weakening activity in selected sectors. Wednesday's October personal consumption expenditures price index increased 0.3% on the month and 3.8% from a year earlier, while annual core inflation accelerated to 3.3% , reinforcing concerns about underlying price pressures. The second estimate of third-quarter gross domestic product indicated that the economy expanded at an annualized 4.3%, while personal income increased 0.7% in October and consumer spending advanced 0.3%. Initial unemployment claims declined to 189,000, suggesting continued resilience in the labor market. However, inflation-adjusted consumer spending was essentially unchanged, indicating that higher prices continued to constrain purchasing power. Friday's post-Thanksgiving session brought no comparable major economic release, leaving investors focused on the implications of Wednesday's data and the outlook for additional Federal Reserve tightening.

items.titleEn: Gold and silver bounce from 15-month lows, but Fed risks loom large
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - After another difficult week, there appears to be some light at the end of the tunnel; however, some analysts note that it could just be the next oncoming train. In a modest recovery, the gold market is ending the week back above $3,600 an ounce. While prices are on track to end the week with a 3% gain, the precious metal rallied as much as 7.5% from its 15-month low reached midweek, hitting $3,685 an ounce on Friday. Meanwhile, silver has seen an even more impressive recovery, rallying more than 16% in less than two days after testing support near $38 an ounce Wednesday and pushing above $44.50 an ounce Friday.

items.titleEn: Gold may get a relief rally following the Fed, but Warsh's tone could still hammer prices lower – BubbleBubble Report's Colombo
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold ’s long decline from its late-January highs is likely over, but the yellow metal will probably remain in a holding pattern until markets get only a 25-basis-point rate hike and a less hawkish tone from the Federal Reserve, according to Jesse Colombo, independent precious metals analyst and founder of the BubbleBubble Report. “$3,200 to $3,500 was exactly the support zone that I delineated this past weekend,” he said. “The reason why it was significant was because that was where gold consolidated in the summer of 2025. From around mid-April until early September, it was in that range, bounced around, and consolidated before launching into that fall 2025 run. And sure enough, we did bounce off of there and it became oversold according to RSI and other oscillators. The stock market bounced as well the past couple days, so that removed some of the downward pressure of liquidations from precious metals, allowing them to have that bounce.” “I see that as being a strong support,” Colombo said. “I highly doubt it's going to drop below there. I don't think it will necessarily have to test down [to the lower edge of the range]. I think [Wednesday] was the test.”

items.titleEn: Gold could ride the double tailwind of equities and seasonals higher into the new year – investingLive's Button
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold prices are now marching in lockstep with equity valuations, and if the yellow metal’s long-running bullish seasonal pattern kicks in, precious metals could be back on the upswing over the medium term, according to Adam Button, head of currency strategy at investingLive. “Correlations have gone to one this week, in terms of equities and gold,” Button said on Friday afternoon. “There was this intense washout in sentiment earlier in the week, and then a surprising turnaround that has really snowballed in the past three days.” Button said one of the most dependable seasonal trends is also due to kick in, with India’s wedding and festival season, the run-up to Christmas, Chinese New Year, and Valentine’s Day. “The seasonals really pick up for gold here from now, and equities as well,” he said. “If those two are going to go together, that’s a double tailwind there.”

items.titleEn: Nasdaq, Dow rise over 500 pts as Anthropic pops 11% to lead AI rebound
items.summaryEn: Buy Anthropic (NASDAQ: ANTHR). The stock is up ~11% and reclaimed above its $83 IPO price after heavy infrastructure/financing fears. This is a clean “de-risking” setup: investors are willing to pay again for AI exposure as the market rotates back into beaten-down growth. Key follow-through catalyst is continued AI sentiment improving alongside semis/data-center names. Key Risk: Another wave of funding/infrastructure cost concerns that forces ANTHR to guide higher spending without matching revenue growth. Buy iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) (or SMH). The article shows broad AI rebound participation: Sandisk, Micron, AMD, Broadcom, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index all surged while the Nasdaq rallied hard. This is second-order breadth: when the whole AI supply chain moves together, it usually signals the market is rotating back into the entire earnings engine, not just one headline stock.

items.titleEn: Selling fatigue and seasonal tailwinds fueling gold's recovery – Saxo Bank
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market, while off its overnight highs, continues to hold its recent gains above $3,600 an ounce. Although prices have seen a solid bounce off their recent 15-month lows, one market strategist said that it might still be too early to call a clear bottom in the market. In a comment to Kitco News, Ole Hansen, Head of Commodity Strategy at Saxo Bank, said gold is benefiting from positive seasonal factors and selling fatigue. He added that it is too soon to tell whether higher prices reflect a shift in short-term fundamentals. In a note Thursday, Hansen pointed out that gold has swung from trading 45% above its 200-day moving average in January to 20% below it this week. He described the recent volatility as the deepest drawdown within a 12-month period since the early 1980s.

items.titleEn: Why Tesla shares jumped 5% on Friday?
items.summaryEn: Buy TSLA. Germany’s antitrust filing to acquire EMAG hints Tesla is securing precision-machining capability for Optimus actuators—exactly the bottleneck for reliable, low-cost mass production. If Tesla can shorten retooling cycles and cut scrap/rework, Optimus economics improve and the market can re-rate TSLA on faster commercialization plus potential supervised-driving EU approval as a near-term catalyst. Key Risk: Tesla can’t integrate EMAG fast enough (or the acquired assets don’t match Optimus needs), so Optimus costs and timelines don’t improve. Buy EMAG. The filing puts EMAG on the radar as a likely acquisition target; even without disclosed assets/pricing, the probability of a deal and deal-related premium tends to lift the stock. If Tesla is serious about actuator machining, EMAG’s core equipment and know-how become more valuable.

items.titleEn: Why Nvidia pared opening gains to decline again on Friday?
items.summaryEn: Sell NVDA. The news stacks three separate threats: (1) Blackwell hardware in a Shanghai facility tied to the Alice Huang controversy raises export-licensing and compliance risk, (2) new US export controls are already forcing Dell/Supermicro to halt shipments of Nvidia-chip servers across Southeast Asia, and (3) CreditWatch Negative signals governance/oversight risk that can lead to a downgrade. Together, this pressures both near-term sales and the multiple. Key Risk: A fast, credible resolution that Nvidia is fully compliant (licenses obtained or hardware use proven legitimate) plus clear guidance that export-control revenue at risk is far smaller than estimates. Sell Super Micro Computer (SMCI). The article names Supermicro as one of the manufacturing partners told to halt shipments of servers containing Nvidia chips to Malaysia/Singapore/Thailand/Indonesia. That’s direct demand disruption for SMCI’s AI server pipeline, and it compounds NVDA-specific compliance/export fears into a broader supply-chain hit.

items.titleEn: Gold will reach $4,600/oz by Q4 2027 as rates fall, USD gives back 10% overvaluation – J.P. Morgan's Tang
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) – Gold prices will likely remain under pressure in the near term as monetary policy continues to tighten, but central bank purchases and demand for the precious metal as a hedge against currency debasement will support gold over the medium term, with prices reaching $4600 by year-end 2027, according to Yuxuan Tang, strategist at J.P. Morgan. “I think over the near term it's going to be tough, because it's not the best environment for gold in a rising yield environment,” she said in a recent interview with CNBC. “And I'm not talking about the day-to-day moves in Treasuries. It's the overall monetary tightening backdrop that is adding pressure to gold.” However, Tang said that conditions will become more favorable for gold in the second half of the coming year.

items.titleEn: What's driving SanDisk stock higher today?
items.summaryEn: Buy SNDK. The Nvidia GB200 rack demo shows AI can use far more NAND via SSD “memory expansion,” and SanDisk already has Kioxia JV coverage through 2034 plus accelerating data-center revenue (+61% QoQ) with fiscal Q2 revenue guidance ($12.2B+). The stock is deeply off YTD highs, so any sustained shipment/margin confirmation can re-rate the name quickly. Key Risk: NAND prices fall hard enough that higher volumes don’t translate into profit growth (margin compression wipes out the earnings rebound). Buy Micron (MU) as a higher-beta way to play the same NAND demand theme. If AI servers truly need more SSD-backed flash capacity, the whole NAND supply chain benefits, and MU is positioned to capture incremental pricing/volume as data-center builds expand.

items.titleEn: Micron, SK Hynix, SanDisk stocks rise but what's the verdict on demand outlook?
items.summaryEn: Buy MU. The article flags oversupply risk, but also notes supply may stay tight into 2028 because capacity is being steered toward AI-focused HBM and manufacturers can cut production to defend LTA pricing. With MU down >35% in a month, the market is pricing a worse demand collapse than the base-case implies; the rebound signals buyers are already positioning for a “not-quite-glut” outcome. Key Risk: Data-center permitting delays turn into a real demand break and prices roll over faster than manufacturers can cut supply. Buy SK Hynix. It’s up ~6% on the day while the core debate is whether AI infrastructure spending persists. Hynix is better positioned than pure-play conventional DRAM because AI systems pull more HBM, and the article explicitly says capacity allocation toward AI can keep conventional supply constrained. If AI capex holds, Hynix should outperform as the market reprices “tight supply longer.”

items.titleEn: Gold rallies above $3,600, silver surges as dollar weakness supports metals - Kitco AM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were sharply higher in early U.S. trading Friday, extending their recovery from recent lows as a softer U.S. dollar, renewed Chinese physical demand and improving global equity sentiment supported precious metals despite persistent expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening. Gold climbed back above $3,600.00 an ounce after falling to its lowest level since September 2025 earlier this week, while silver posted substantially stronger gains as bargain hunting and renewed speculative demand accelerated the rebound. Reduced trading activity following Thursday's U.S. Thanksgiving holiday also helped ease the liquidation pressure that had weighed on bullion during the recent equity market selloff. Spot gold was trading near $3,649.60 an ounce, up $84.10, or 2.36%, while silver was trading near $43.640, up approximately $2.230, or 5.37%, on the session. Gold had traded between $3,569.60 and $3,686.00 during the day, while silver's range extended from $41.630 to $44.690. Wednesday's U.S. economic releases reinforced expectations for restrictive Federal Reserve monetary policy as stronger-than-expected economic growth coincided with persistent underlying inflation. The October personal consumption expenditures price index increased 0.3% on the month and 3.8% from a year earlier, while core PCE inflation, excluding food and energy, accelerated to 3.3% annually. The second estimate of third-quarter gross domestic product was revised higher to an annualized 4.3%, indicating continued economic resilience despite elevated borrowing costs. Personal income increased 0.7% in October, while consumer spending advanced 0.3%, although inflation-adjusted spending was essentially unchanged. Initial unemployment claims declined to 189,000, suggesting continued resilience in the labor market, while durable goods orders increased just 0.2%. The stronger growth and inflation figures reinforced expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening, although Friday's recovery in precious metals suggested that easing dollar strength and reduced selling pressure were temporarily offsetting the impact of higher expected interest rates.

items.titleEn: Why are CoreWeave and Nebius stocks soaring despite mounting debt risks?
items.summaryEn: Buy CRWV. The key catalyst is a $4.5B Meta-linked loan at ~7–7.5% secured by GPUs and tied to Meta demand—far cheaper than ~18% bond yields. That signals lenders believe cash flows are contract-backed, and it can quickly reduce near-term refinancing stress. The stock’s rebound after heavy shorting also gives upside momentum if the market starts pricing the cheaper funding path. Key Risk: The loan terms fall apart or Meta-linked collateral doesn’t translate into real repayment coverage, forcing CRWV back into high-cost refinancing. Buy NBIS. Management expects $17–$20B of customer prepayments in 2027 plus contract-backed borrowing to cover most of $40–$45B capex, leaving a smaller funding gap. With a cash cushion (~$7.4B), the market can re-rate NBIS if investors believe prepayments are durable and not delayed.
